name: SMR-Metal Technology
old_description: At SMR, our team is ready to work with you to meet all of your manufacturing needs. Locally based in South Windsor CT, our
about:
SMR-Metal Technology operates from South Windsor, Connecticut, where it produces metal fabrications and assemblies for a range of industrial sectors. The company emphasizes that its parts are professionally and completely made in the United States.

The shop provides the entire manufacturing and fabrication process under one roof. Starting from CNC laser cutting, the team cuts, punches, bends, sands, deburrs, and mills parts, then joins them with both MIG and TIG welding before final assembly. Special finishes such as powder coating, painting, and plating are available on request. Materials handled include steel, stainless steel, aluminum, brass, and copper.

Its customer base spans automotive, locomotive, aerospace, medical, energy, marine, defense, communications, restaurant customization, and original equipment manufacturing (OEM) sectors. The company works from customer sketches or samples at any stage of the design process.

SMR positions itself as a single-source partner that can take a project from concept through finished part, offering both fabrication and finishing services without requiring the customer to manage multiple vendors.

name: SON Metal Fab
old_description: With the strong support of his family, Butch Harrison founded Specialty’s Our Name, now proudly known as
about:
SON Metal Fab operates from Ashland, Virginia, just north of Richmond. The business traces its roots to Butch Harrison, who founded the company—originally named Specialty's Our Name—with strong family support. While the exact founding year is not publicly disclosed, the firm cites three decades of industry experience.

The shop provides custom sheet metal fabrication, laser cutting, precision parts, welding, rolling, deburring, CNC punching, CNC bending, and powder coating. Its equipment includes a ¼″–10′ AccurShear with CNC controls, a Hurco CNC lathe with bar feeder, and a Hurco machining center, enabling combined fabrication, welding, and machining under one roof. The company describes its comprehensive services as tailored to the specific needs of a broad client base.

The company serves clients in and around Richmond, Virginia, addressing both short- and long-term project needs. Its experienced project managers are available to assist with drafting and prototyping for new projects, helping to move concepts into production quickly.

Harrison's founding emphasis on workmanship remains central: the firm highlights its dedication to quality craftsmanship and attention to detail as the basis for delivering products that consistently meet or exceed client expectations.

name: SPF ELECTRIC
old_description: A Leading Provider of Electrical Materials for Manufacturers, Installers & Contractors.
about:
SPF Electric, LLC operates from Angleton, Texas, on the Gulf Coast. The company does not publish a founding year, but its own materials cite over 25 years of immersion in the electrical power sector and nearly two decades of experience. No individual founders are named in the source content, and ownership structure (family, veteran, woman-owned, etc.) is not disclosed.

The shop specializes in electrical manufacturing and fabrication, offering bus fabrication (precision cutting, bending, punching, and shearing of copper and aluminum bus bar, plus aluminum bus bar welding), switchgear fabrication (CNC cutting, vertical and horizontal press brakes, iron worker, welding, and stud welding), G10/GP03 component machining (barriers, bus supports, circuit breaker operating rods), relay panels and switchgear doors, and powder coating. All services — design, drafting, fabrication, powder coating, gasket installation, and hardware assembly — are performed in-house, which the company says enables quicker turnarounds.

SPF Electric serves industrial, petrochemical, and electrical testing markets, with a noted focus on the Texas Gulf Coast area. Customers include maintenance and engineering departments needing replacement or custom doors, panels, covers, and structural components for switchgear, motor control centers (MCCs), and transformers. The company also highlights reverse engineering of hundreds of such components.

The firm emphasizes that centralizing design, fabrication, and finishing under one roof reduces lead times and improves quality. It also promotes its reverse-engineering capability and extensive library of factory drawings for relays, lights, switches, latches, push buttons, and accessories as a way to solve challenges for modern maintenance and engineering teams.

name: SPI Semicon
old_description: At SPI/Semicon, we manufacture semiconductor packaging solutions as advanced as the wafers they protect.
about:
SPI Semicon operates from Ogden, Utah, tracing its roots to 1970 when two industry leaders — Semicon Systems and Semiconductor Products — merged to form the company. The combined entity brought together decades of packaging expertise under one roof, establishing a foundation that now spans facilities in the United States and the Philippines.

The company manufactures advanced semiconductor packaging solutions that cover the full spectrum from front-end wafer fabrication to back-end finished devices. Core processes include vacuum forming, extrusion, die-cutting, and injection molding, with the ability to produce custom-made parts tailored to specific device requirements. Its ISO 9001‑certified quality management system governs every production step, ensuring traceability and repeatability across both domestic and overseas sites.

SPI Semicon serves the semiconductor industry exclusively, supplying packaging components that meet or exceed EIA‑541 and ESD 5.11.1 standards for resistivity and static protection. Customers range from wafer fabs and assembly houses to original equipment manufacturers seeking reliable, high‑performance packaging for logic, memory, and power devices.

The company was built on a commitment to innovation and precision, positioning its packaging as "as advanced as the wafers they protect." Leadership emphasizes that deep engineering expertise, unique product designs, and a service‑first culture are what differentiate SPI Semicon in a market where reliability and consistency are non‑negotiable.

name: STI Electronics, Inc.
old_description: STI Electronics, Inc. is a leading provider of comprehensive solder and electronic assembly training, designed to enhance skills and meet the stringent requirements of the industry.
about:
STI Electronics, Inc. is headquartered in Madison, Alabama. The company was founded in 1982 by Jim D. Raby, P.E., in San Dimas, California, as a family-run business. It relocated to Madison in 1993 and has since grown to employ over fifty professionals.

The firm provides electronic contract manufacturing, engineering services, analytical testing, and IPC-authorized training. Its manufacturing capabilities include PCB assembly (surface-mount and through-hole), rapid prototyping, new product introduction builds, design-for-manufacturing review, rework and repair, conformal coating and encapsulation, and both leaded and lead-free soldering. Operations are supported by cleanroom facilities, failure-analysis labs, and materials-testing equipment at sites in Madison and Houston, Texas.

STI serves customers in aerospace, defense, medical, industrial, and energy markets, focusing on safety-critical and military-grade applications where precision and reliability are paramount. Its client base includes original equipment manufacturers and prime contractors requiring engineering-driven, low-to-medium volume production.

Raby’s background in developing NASA and Department of Defense soldering schools established a culture of technical rigor that remains central to STI’s differentiation. The company combines advanced manufacturing, analytical laboratories, and one of the industry’s most respected training programs under one roof to help customers reduce risk and solve complex manufacturing challenges.
